data.title: We Don’t Think Kody Technolab's (NSE:KODYTECH) Earnings Should Make Shareholders Too Comfortable
data.description:
Kody Technolab Limited's (NSE:KODYTECH) stock performed strongly after the recent earnings report. Investors should be cautious however, as there some causes of concern deeper in the numbers.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Zooming In On Kody Technolab's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Kody Technolab recorded an accrual ratio of 0.46. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. And indeed, during the period the company didn't produce any free cash flow whatsoever. Even though it reported a profit of ₹174.9m, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through ₹599m in the last year. We also note that Kody Technolab's free cash flow was actually negative last year as well, so we could understand if shareholders were bothered by its outflow of ₹599m. Notably, the company has issued new shares, thus diluting existing shareholders and reducing their share of future earnings.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Kody Technolab.

One essential aspect of assessing earnings quality is to look at how much a company is diluting shareholders. In fact, Kody Technolab increased the number of shares on issue by 12% over the last twelve months by issuing new shares. Therefore, each share now receives a smaller portion of profit. To celebrate net income while ignoring dilution is like rejoicing because you have a single slice of a larger pizza, but ignoring the fact that the pizza is now cut into many more slices. You can see a chart of Kody Technolab's EPS by clicking here.

How Is Dilution Impacting Kody Technolab's Earnings Per Share (EPS)?

Kody Technolab has improved its profit over the last three years, with an annualized gain of 241% in that time. But EPS was only up 187% per year, in the exact same period. And at a glance the 47% gain in profit over the last year impresses. But in comparison, EPS only increased by 24% over the same period. So you can see that the dilution has had a bit of an impact on shareholders.

In the long term, earnings per share growth should beget share price growth. So Kody Technolab shareholders will want to see that EPS figure continue to increase. However, if its profit increases while its earnings per share stay flat (or even fall) then shareholders might not see much benefit. For the ordinary retail shareholder, EPS is a great measure to check your hypothetical "share" of the company's profit.

Our Take On Kody Technolab's Profit Performance

As it turns out, Kody Technolab couldn't match its profit with cashflow and its dilution means that earnings per share growth is lagging net income growth. For the reasons mentioned above, we think that a perfunctory glance at Kody Technolab's statutory profits might make it look better than it really is on an underlying level. If you'd like to know more about Kody Technolab as a business, it's important to be aware of any risks it's facing. For example - Kody Technolab has 1 warning sign we think you should be aware of.

data.title: We Think Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands' (NSE:ABLBL) Robust Earnings Are Conservative
data.description:
Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (NSE:ABLBL) just reported healthy earnings but the stock price didn't move much. We think that investors have missed some encouraging factors underlying the profit figures.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands' Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

For the year to September 2026, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands had an accrual ratio of -0.34. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. To wit, it produced free cash flow of ₹10.0b during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of ₹2.06b. Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands' year-on-year free cash flow was as flat as two-day-old fizzy drink.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands' Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Because of this, we think Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands' underlying earnings potential is as good as, or possibly even better, than the statutory profit makes it seem! And on top of that, its earnings per share increased by 53% in the last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. So while earnings quality is important, it's equally important to consider the risks facing Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands at this point in time. data.title: TeraWulf (WULF) Funds Muskie Data Campus Infrastructure And Winter Bill Credits
data.description:
• TeraWulf (NasdaqCM:WULF) agreed a new partnership with Kentucky Power to support the planned Muskie Data Campus infrastructure buildout.
  • The arrangement includes TeraWulf funding new generation and transmission assets tied to the Muskie Data Campus development in Kentucky.
  • The deal also provides winter bill credits for eligible Kentucky Power customers funded by TeraWulf as part of the partnership.
  • The Muskie Data Campus funding and bill credit agreement is only one part of the broader TeraWulf story investors are weighing. Our analysis turns up 4 warning signs (1 major) for TeraWulf as well.

AI compute buildouts continue to attract capital, so it can be worth comparing this agreement with other infrastructure focused plays in 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

TeraWulf runs and develops digital infrastructure in the US, so this Kentucky Power agreement plugs directly into its role as a builder and operator of large scale compute sites. With a reported market value of about $6.5 billion, the business already sits at a size where utility partnerships can shape how new facilities are structured and funded.

1 thing going right for TeraWulf that this headline doesn't cover.

How the Kentucky Power deal feeds TeraWulf’s AI lease story

TeraWulf’s investment story hinges on whether it can turn scarce, long term power access into contracted AI and high performance computing leases at scale. This Kentucky Power partnership goes straight to that premise because Muskie’s economics rely on reliable electricity and predictable funding rather than short cycle bitcoin revenue.

The main requirement is successful delivery of large, power secured campuses on time and on budget, despite higher project costs and tight electrical labor markets...

See how the full story points towards a $31.17 fair value for TeraWulf.

This agreement supports the bullish view that power constraints are a gating factor for AI data centers. By underwriting Muskie’s generation and transmission assets and accepting bill credit obligations, TeraWulf is trying to secure electricity in a way rivals like Marathon Digital or Core Scientific often depend on third parties for.

The bear case is that every new power partnership adds complexity to a build program where analysts already flag cost inflation, a widening year to date net loss of US$657.64 million, and less than one year of cash runway. If Muskie runs over budget or underutilizes its contracted power, the same deal that confirms access to energy could pressure returns and funding flexibility.

The upshot is that this single partnership can read as validation or as added strain, depending on whether your TeraWulf narrative emphasizes contracted AI leases or build out risk.
